description: Building a working compiler for a small language, phase by phase: lexing, parsing, syntax trees, semantic analysis, intermediate code, optimisation and code generation for a real or virtual machine. Taught to the depth of a leading compilers course.
modelledOn: Aho, Lam, Sethi and Ullman, Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools
Appel, Modern Compiler Implementation in Java/C/ML
Cooper and Torczon, Engineering a Compiler
outcomes: Specify tokens with regular expressions and build a lexer by hand and with a generator.
Write grammars, eliminate ambiguity and left recursion, and build recursive-descent, LL(1) and LR parsers.
Construct abstract syntax trees and perform semantic analysis with symbol tables and type checking.
Translate to intermediate representations such as three-address code and SSA.
Apply local and global optimisations driven by dataflow analysis.
Generate code with instruction selection, register allocation and runtime support, and test the compiler end to end.

units.title: Overview of compilation
topics: Compilers, interpreters, JIT compilers and transpilers; the phases and their data structures
The source language for the course (a small C-like or Pascal-like language) and the target (RISC-V, x86 or a VM)
Bootstrapping, cross-compilation, the toolchain (assembler, linker, loader)
Project setup: test suite, driver, error reporting conventions

units.title: Lexical analysis
topics: Tokens, lexemes, patterns; keywords, identifiers, literals, comments, whitespace
Regular expressions to NFA (Thompson), NFA to DFA (subset construction), DFA minimisation
Hand-written scanners versus generators (lex/flex, ANTLR); longest match and lookahead
Error recovery in the lexer; Unicode and source positions for error messages

units.title: Parsing: top-down
topics: Context-free grammars, derivations, parse trees, ambiguity; precedence and associativity in grammars
Eliminating left recursion and left factoring; FIRST and FOLLOW sets
Recursive-descent parsing; predictive LL(1) table-driven parsing
Error recovery: panic mode, synchronising tokens; good error messages
Pratt parsing for expressions

units.title: Parsing: bottom-up
topics: Shift-reduce parsing, handles, conflicts
LR(0) items and automaton, SLR, LR(1), LALR(1) table construction
Parser generators (yacc/bison, ANTLR); resolving conflicts with precedence declarations
Comparing LL and LR; generalised and PEG parsing in brief

units.title: Abstract syntax trees
topics: Concrete versus abstract syntax; designing AST node classes
Building the AST during parsing; semantic actions and syntax-directed translation
Tree traversal with the visitor pattern; pretty printing and AST dumps for debugging
Attribute grammars: synthesised and inherited attributes

units.title: Semantic analysis and symbol tables
topics: Scopes, declarations, name resolution; symbol table design with nested scopes
Type systems: type expressions, equivalence, coercion, overloading; type checking expressions, statements and functions
Semantic checks: declared before use, break inside loop, return paths, constant expressions
Type inference in brief; error reporting and recovery

units.title: Intermediate code and runtime environments
topics: Three-address code, quadruples, control-flow graphs; translating expressions, control flow (short-circuit booleans), arrays and records
Static single assignment form and its construction
Runtime organisation: activation records, calling conventions, stack frames, parameter passing, nested functions
Heap management and garbage collection basics; exceptions

units.title: Optimisation
topics: Local optimisations: constant folding, algebraic simplification, common subexpression elimination, copy propagation, dead code
Dataflow analysis: reaching definitions, live variables, available expressions; the iterative framework
Global optimisations: global CSE, loop-invariant code motion, strength reduction, induction variables
Peephole optimisation; inlining; introduction to LLVM passes

units.title: Code generation
topics: Instruction selection: tree pattern matching, simple macro expansion
Register allocation: liveness, interference graphs, graph colouring, spilling; linear scan
Instruction scheduling and target-specific details; generating assembly and linking with a runtime
End-to-end: compiling and running test programs; performance comparison against a reference compiler
